relating to the kneecap

en.correct: describing an amputation level that occurs through the long bones of the midfoot, preserving the heel and part of the arch
distractors: describing an amputation level that occurs through the ankle joint
describing an amputation level that occurs through the toe joints only

example.text: A transmetatarsal amputation left him with a shortened but functional foot for partial foot prosthetics.

en.correct: the surgical removal of a toe or finger together with all or part of its corresponding long bone in the foot or hand
distractors: the removal of an entire limb through a joint
the removal of skin and soft tissue only, preserving all bones

example.text: A ray amputation of the fifth toe preserved more of the foot's weight-bearing surface than a full transmetatarsal cut.

en.correct: a prosthetic component that replaces missing toes and fills the front of a shoe to maintain balance and appearance after a partial foot amputation
distractors: a rigid brace worn to correct hammer toe deformities
a cushioned pad placed inside a below-knee socket

example.text: The toe filler restored a natural shoe fit after his partial foot amputation.

en.correct: a brace that spans the ankle and foot to support, align, or assist their movement, typically worn inside a shoe
distractors: a prosthesis that fully replaces a missing foot and ankle
a brace that spans the knee and ankle only

example.text: The ankle-foot orthosis prevented foot drop during the swing phase of her gait.

en.correct: a brace that spans the knee, ankle, and foot to support or control movement across all three joints
distractors: a brace limited to the ankle and foot joints
a prosthesis that replaces the entire lower limb

example.text: He was fitted with a knee-ankle-foot orthosis to stabilize his leg after the nerve injury.

en.correct: a technique that applies controlled electrical pulses to paralyzed or weakened muscles to produce functional movement, such as during walking
distractors: a technique that records muscle signals to control a myoelectric prosthesis
a surgical method for redirecting nerves to new muscle targets

example.text: Functional electrical stimulation triggered his ankle muscles to lift the foot during each step.

en.correct: a device that interfaces with the nervous system to restore or replace a lost sensory or motor function
distractors: a prosthesis that replaces a missing limb using only mechanical linkages
a socket lined with pressure-sensing pads

example.text: The neuroprosthesis relayed sensory information directly to nerves in his residual limb.

en.correct: an implanted device that electrically stimulates remaining retinal cells to restore a limited degree of vision
distractors: an external device that magnifies images for people with low vision
a hearing device implanted in the inner ear

example.text: The retinal prosthesis allowed him to perceive patterns of light and dark after years of blindness.

en.correct: a device implanted on or within a peripheral nerve to record signals from, or deliver stimulation to, that nerve for prosthetic control or sensory feedback
distractors: a socket component that grips the residual limb's outer surface
a surface electrode taped onto the skin over a muscle

example.text: The peripheral nerve interface let him feel simulated touch through his prosthetic fingertips.

en.correct: relating to feedback delivered through vibration sensed by the skin
distractors: relating to feedback delivered through electrical current felt as tingling
relating to feedback delivered through changes in socket pressure alone

example.text: A vibrotactile motor on his forearm buzzed harder as his prosthetic hand gripped more tightly.

en.correct: pain caused by a stimulus that would not normally provoke pain, such as light touch
distractors: an increased pain response to a stimulus that is normally painful
complete loss of sensation in an area of skin

example.text: Allodynia around his incision made even the liner's light contact feel painful at first.

en.correct: an unpleasant, abnormal sensation such as burning or tingling, often occurring spontaneously in a residual limb
distractors: the complete absence of sensation in a limb
a normal sensation of pressure from a well-fitted socket

example.text: He described a burning dysesthesia along the incision line that worsened at night.

en.correct: an older term for a severe, persistent burning pain following nerve injury, now generally classified under complex regional pain syndrome
distractors: a mild, temporary soreness following a new socket fitting
numbness resulting from prolonged pressure on a nerve

example.text: Historical case reports of causalgia after limb injury described burning pain out of proportion to the wound.

en.correct: a thickened, wart-like overgrowth of skin that can develop on a residual limb from chronic irritation or poor socket fit
distractors: a smooth, painless swelling caused by fluid buildup under the liner
a thinning of the skin from prolonged pressure

example.text: Verrucous hyperplasia developed at the distal end of his limb where the socket fit poorly.

en.correct: a force that acts parallel to a surface, such as skin against a socket wall, rather than perpendicular to it, and is a major cause of skin breakdown
distractors: a force that pushes straight into a surface, compressing the tissue beneath it
the total weight transmitted through a prosthesis during standing

example.text: Excessive shear stress at the socket brim led to a friction blister within days.

en.correct: an instrument used to measure the hardness of a material, such as a prosthetic liner or foot cushion
distractors: an instrument used to measure the electrical resistance of a myoelectric signal
an instrument used to measure limb circumference

example.text: The manufacturer used a durometer to confirm the liner's gel met the specified softness.

en.correct: describing a material that exhibits both viscous and elastic behavior, deforming under load and gradually returning to shape over time
distractors: describing a material that is perfectly rigid and does not deform under load
describing a material that shatters rather than bends under stress

example.text: The viscoelastic gel liner slowly conformed to the shape of his residual limb throughout the day.

en.correct: describing a material capable of being softened by heat and molded into a new shape
distractors: describing a material that cannot be reshaped once manufactured
describing a material that conducts electrical signals

example.text: The clinic kept a supply of thermoformable sheets for fabricating quick check sockets.

en.correct: the late portion of the stance phase of gait, occurring as the body's weight moves ahead of the supporting foot before push-off
distractors: the moment the heel first contacts the ground
the portion of the gait cycle when the foot is airborne

example.text: The prosthetic foot's keel released stored energy during terminal stance to assist forward propulsion.

en.correct: the instant in the gait cycle when the foot first touches the ground, beginning the stance phase
distractors: the instant the foot leaves the ground to begin swing phase
the midpoint of stance when the body passes directly over the foot

example.text: A softer heel wedge softened the impact felt at initial contact.

en.correct: the final portion of stance phase, immediately before the foot lifts off the ground to begin swing phase
distractors: the initial portion of stance phase, right after the foot touches down
the midpoint of swing phase when the leg is directly beneath the hip

example.text: During pre-swing, the prosthetic knee began to unlock in preparation for the swing phase.

en.correct: the early portion of stance phase in which the body's weight is transferred fully onto the newly planted foot
distractors: the final portion of stance phase before toe-off
the portion of swing phase when the leg accelerates forward

example.text: The microprocessor knee added extra resistance during loading response to prevent buckling.

en.correct: the phase of gait in which the body's weight passes directly over the supporting foot
distractors: the phase of gait immediately following heel contact
the phase of gait when the foot is swinging through the air

example.text: He felt the most stable during midstance, when his weight was centered over the prosthetic foot.

en.correct: the point in the gait cycle at which the toes leave the ground, ending stance phase and beginning swing phase
distractors: the point at which the heel first touches the ground
the point at which body weight is centered over the foot

example.text: A responsive keel gave him a noticeable push at toe-off.

en.correct: the custom-molded portion of a prosthesis that encloses and interfaces directly with the residual limb
distractors: the mechanical joint that allows a prosthetic knee to bend
the outer cosmetic cover that gives a limb a lifelike appearance

example.text: The prosthetist reshaped the socket after the patient's residual limb changed volume.

en.correct: a myoelectric control strategy in which the speed or force of a prosthetic movement varies with the strength of the muscle signal
distractors: a control strategy in which movement speed is fixed regardless of signal strength
a control strategy based solely on mechanical cable tension

example.text: With proportional control, a stronger muscle contraction closed the hand more quickly.

en.correct: to build up layers of resin-impregnated fabric over a mold to form a rigid prosthetic socket or component
distractors: to remove excess plaster from a cast before it fully hardens
to record electrical activity from a residual muscle

example.text: The technician began to laminate the socket, layering carbon fiber sleeves over the positive model.

en.correct: a clear, temporary test socket used to evaluate fit and alignment before fabricating the final socket
distractors: a padded liner worn permanently inside the definitive socket
a rigid dressing applied in the operating room after surgery

example.text: The clear check socket let the prosthetist see pressure areas on the skin as the patient stood.

en.correct: a cushioned component placed at the bottom of a prosthetic socket to protect the sensitive end of the residual limb
distractors: a strap that wraps around the top of the socket for suspension
a rigid plate that anchors the pylon to the socket

example.text: A softer distal end pad relieved the pressure he felt at the tip of his residual limb.

en.correct: an instrument used to measure the angle of a joint, such as during a range-of-motion assessment
distractors: an instrument used to measure the hardness of a liner material
an instrument used to record muscle electrical activity

example.text: The clinician used a goniometer to measure the residual knee's flexion contracture.

en.correct: an instrument used to measure force or strength, such as grip force produced through a prosthetic hand
distractors: an instrument used to measure the angle of a joint
an instrument used to detect electrical crosstalk between muscles

example.text: A dynamometer confirmed the myoelectric hand could generate enough grip force to hold a cup.

en.correct: a sensor that converts mechanical force into an electrical signal, used to measure the load passing through a prosthetic limb
distractors: a sensor that measures the electrical activity of a muscle
a battery module that powers a myoelectric prosthesis

example.text: Researchers embedded a load cell in the pylon to record forces during each step.

en.correct: a sensor that measures the amount a material deforms under load, often used to monitor stress on prosthetic components
distractors: a sensor that measures skin temperature inside a socket
a sensor that detects the angle of a prosthetic knee

example.text: A strain gauge bonded to the pylon revealed unexpectedly high bending forces during stair descent.

en.correct: a surgical technique that redirects sensory nerves from an amputated limb to skin on another body area, allowing touch there to be perceived as coming from the missing limb
distractors: a surgical technique that anchors muscle directly to the end of a bone
a technique that fits electrodes onto the skin without surgery

example.text: After targeted sensory reinnervation, touching his chest produced sensations he felt as coming from his missing hand.

en.correct: a set of multiple electrical contacts surgically placed within or on nerve or muscle tissue to record signals or deliver stimulation
distractors: a single surface sensor taped onto the skin over a muscle
a battery pack implanted to power a prosthetic limb

example.text: The implantable electrode array recorded signals from several muscle groups simultaneously.

en.correct: an electrode that wraps around a peripheral nerve to record its signals or deliver stimulation without penetrating the nerve fibers
distractors: an electrode that penetrates directly through nerve fibers
a surface electrode adhered to intact skin

example.text: The cuff electrode encircled the median nerve to relay sensory feedback to the prosthetic hand.

en.correct: a regenerative electrode with small perforations through which severed nerve fibers regrow, allowing a highly selective interface for recording or stimulation
distractors: an electrode taped onto the skin above a target muscle
an electrode that wraps around a nerve without penetrating it

example.text: Nerve fibers regenerated through the sieve electrode's tiny openings over several months.

en.correct: a fabrication process in which a heated thermoplastic sheet is drawn tightly around a mold using suction to create a socket or orthotic shell
distractors: a process that bonds resin-soaked fabric layers over a mold under pressure
a process that mills a socket shape from a solid block of plastic

example.text: Vacuum forming pulled the softened plastic sheet snugly against every contour of the positive model.

en.correct: a liquid polymer that hardens to bind layers of fabric together, forming the rigid shell of a laminated prosthetic socket
distractors: a soft gel used to line the inside of a socket
a lubricant applied to ease donning a liner

example.text: He poured the lamination resin over the fabric layers and let it cure overnight.

en.correct: the process of arranging layers of carbon-fiber fabric in specific orientations before resin infusion, to control the strength and flexibility of a finished component
distractors: the process of trimming a finished socket to its final edge
the process of grinding a plastic sheet to a smooth finish

example.text: The engineer adjusted the carbon-fiber lay-up to give the running blade more spring in one direction.

en.correct: the vertical distance between a prosthetic foot and the ground during the swing phase of gait, needed to avoid tripping
distractors: the total distance a limb travels during one full stride
the amount of cushioning built into a prosthetic heel

example.text: Insufficient knee flexion during swing left him with too little ground clearance, causing frequent stumbles.

en.correct: softening and breakdown of skin caused by prolonged exposure to moisture, such as trapped sweat inside a socket
distractors: thickening and hardening of skin from repeated friction
loss of sensation in skin due to nerve damage

example.text: Sweat trapped inside the liner led to maceration on the underside of his residual limb.

en.correct: an abnormal thickening of the outer layer of skin, often developing over areas of chronic pressure inside a prosthetic socket
distractors: an abnormal thinning of the skin over a bony prominence
a buildup of fluid beneath the skin surface

example.text: Hyperkeratosis had formed over the area where the socket wall pressed most firmly.

en.correct: a complication of vacuum or suction suspension in which soft tissue swells at the socket's proximal brim while blood flow is restricted distally, causing painful swelling and skin changes at the limb's end
distractors: a suspension failure in which the socket repeatedly slips off the limb
an infection that develops around a percutaneous abutment

example.text: Choke syndrome developed after the socket brim was left too tight for his changing limb volume.
